Rashi on Sukkah 26a:10:1.hebrew: תרתי או תלת - שתים או שלש פעמים יתן לתוך פיו — מורשייל"ש:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:10:1.english: Two or three - Two or three times he puts [food] into his mouth — *morceles* [morsels].

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:10:2.hebrew: כדטעים בר בי רב ועייל לכלה - בבוקר, כשהולכין לבית המדרש, ודואג שמא ימשכו השמועות, וטועם מלא פיו ושותה:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:10:2.english: Like [what] a student of the academy tastes and enters the kallah [lecture] - In the morning, when they go to the house of study, and he is concerned lest the discourses be prolonged, and [so] he tastes a mouthful and drinks.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:11:1.english: He fall asleep - Lest sleep overtake him and he sleep a regular sleep.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:12:1.english: But not substantial sleep - Lest he pass gas [while wearing] them:

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:12:2.hebrew: מוסר שינתו לאחר - אומר לחברו: אם ארדם, העירני:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:12:2.english: [One who] entrusts his sleep to another - He says to his fellow: "If I fall asleep, wake me."

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:13:1.english: Your guarantor requires a guarantor - Lest he too lie down and sleep.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:13:2.english: Between his knees - For he will certainly not fall into a deep sleep.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:13:3.hebrew: רבא אמר - לשמא ירדם לא חיישינן, הלכך בתפילין שרי. וסוכה, היינו טעמא דאסור שינת עראי — לפי שאין קבע לשינה, ואין בה חילוק בין קבע לעראי לענין סוכה, שאין אדם קובע עצמו לשינה, שפעמים שאינו אלא מנמנם מעט ודיו בכך, הלכך זו היא שינתו. וגבי תפילין, דטעמא שמא יפיח בהם ולאו משום איסור שינה — בניים פורתא לא אתי לידי הפחה:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:13:3.english: Rava said - We are not concerned lest he fall into a deep sleep; therefore, with phylacteries it is permitted. And [with regard to] the sukka, this is the reason that casual sleep is forbidden: because there is no fixed [standard] for sleep, and there is no distinction in it between regular and casual regarding the sukka, for a person does not fix himself for sleep, as sometimes he merely dozes a little and that is sufficient for him; therefore, this is his sleep. And regarding phylacteries, where the reason [for the restriction] is lest he pass gas in them, and not because of a prohibition of sleep [itself] — when he dozes a little, he will not come to pass gas.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:1.hebrew: דנקיט להו בידיה - לא קבע ולא עראי, שמא יפלו מידו:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:1.english: Where he holds them in his hand - Neither substantial [sleep] nor a brief [nap] [is permitted], lest they fall from his hand.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:2.hebrew: דמנחי ברישיה - עראי מותר, וקבע אסור, שמא יפיח:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:2.english: Where they are placed on his head - A brief [nap] is permitted, and substantial [sleep] is prohibited, lest he break wind.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:3.hebrew: דפריס סודרא עלייהו - הניחם אצל מראשותיו, בין קבע בין עראי, דלא נתנה תורה למלאכי השרת:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:14:3.english: Where he spreads a cloth over them - He placed them beside his head, [and sleep is permitted,] whether substantial or brief, for the Torah was not given to ministering angels.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:15:1.english: And experiences a seminal emission - He must remove them from his head while the seminal emission is upon him.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:1:1.hebrew: משום ר' שילא אמרו חתן פטור - מקריאת שמע, דטריד, ושאר בני חופה חייבין. ולית להו להני תנאי: העוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:1:1.english: In the name of Rabbi Sheila they said: A groom is exempt - From the recitation of Shema, because he is preoccupied; and the rest of the members of the wedding party are obligated. And these Tannaim do not hold [that] one who is engaged in a mitzva is exempt from [another] mitzva.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:2:1.english: Their merchants - Those who purchase from them in order to sell and make them available to whoever needs them.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:2:2.english: Sellers of sky-blue dye - For ritual fringes.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:1.hebrew: הולכי דרכים ביום פטורין מן הסוכה ביום - דכתיב: ״בסוכות תשבו״ — כעין ישיבת ביתו. כשם שכל השנה אינו נמנע מלכת בדרך בסחורה, כך כל ימות החג שאינו יום טוב, לא הצריכו הכתוב למנוע:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:1.english: Travelers during the day are exempt from the sukka during the day - For it is written: “You shall dwell in sukkot” — [meaning] in the manner of dwelling in his home. Just as throughout the year he does not refrain from traveling on the road for commerce, so too, all the days of the Festival that are not Yom Tov, Scripture did not require him to refrain.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:2.hebrew: הולכים לדבר מצוה פטורין ביום ובלילה - אף על פי שאין הולכין אלא ביום, ומשום דטרידים ודואגים במחשבת המצוה ובתיקוניה, פטורין מן המצוה:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:2.english: Those who travel for a matter of mitzva are exempt by day and at night - Even though they travel only during the day, and because they are preoccupied and concerned with thoughts of the mitzva and its preparations, they are exempt from the mitzva [of sukka].

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:3.english: The bank - On the bank of the river.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:3:4.english: We are emissaries of a mitzva - For we have come to hear the discourse and to greet the Exilarch.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:5:1.english: Guardians of gardens and orchards - They do not move from there.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:5:2.hebrew: כעין תדורו - כדרך שהוא דר כל השנה בביתו, הזקיקתו תורה להניח דירתו ולדור כאן בסוכה, עם מטותיו וכלי תשמישו ומצעותיו. וזה אינו יכול להביאן שם מפני הטורח:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:5:2.english: As you dwell - Just as he dwells all year in his house, the Torah obligated him to leave his dwelling and dwell here in the sukkah, with his beds, his utensils, and his bedding; and this [guardian] is unable to bring them there due to the exertion.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:6:1.hebrew: פרצה קוראה לגנב - משל הדיוט הוא. ואף כאן, הגנב רואה אותו יושב בסוכה בלילה, והוא נכנס וגונב הפירות לרוח אחרת:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:6:1.english: A breach summons the thief - It is a popular proverb. And here too, the thief sees him sitting in the sukkah at night, and he enters and steals the fruit from another direction.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:6:2.hebrew: כריא דפירי - כרי של פירות, שהוא תמיד לפניו ויכול לשומרן, ואין כאן פרצה קוראה לגנב:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:6:2.english: A pile of fruit - A pile of fruit, which is always in front of him and he can guard it, and there is no “breach summons the thief” here.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:7:1.hebrew: רבי יוסי בריבי - יוסי החכם, חריף שבדורו, והוא ר' יוסי בן חלפתא:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:7:1.english: Rabbi Yosei beribbi - Yosei the sage, the sharpest of his generation; and he is Rabbi Yosei ben Ḥalafta.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:8:1.hebrew: למגנא בכילתא - ואע"פ שיש לה גג וגבוהה עשרה, והוי כאילו חוץ לסוכה:
Rashi on Sukkah 26a:8:1.english: To sleep beneath a canopy - Even though it has a roof and is ten [handbreadths] high, and it is as if [he is] outside the sukkah.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:8:2.english: Due to gnats - [That is,] cinceles [Old French for gnats].

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:8:3.english: The foul odor of the gargishta - White earth with which they would plaster the floor of the sukkah.

Rashi on Sukkah 26a:9:1.english: One who suffers - That the sukkah causes him discomfort.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:10:1.hebrew: תרתי (או) תלת - פירש בקונט': שתים או שלש פעמים יתן לתוך פיו, מורשי"ל בלע"ז. ויש ספרים שכתוב בהן "תרתי תלת ביעי", והכל אחד — כדמוכח לקמן גבי "לימא תיהוי תיובתיה דרב יוסף ואביי", דשיעור בית הבליעה כביצה. ולבסוף מסיק: "כדטעים צורבא מדרבנן ואזיל לכלה", שזה מלא פיו, דהיינו כביצה. ושיעור זה דוקא בפת, דפירי לאו בעו סוכה, כדמסיק פרק בתרא דיומא (דף עט: ושם), דקבע דידהו כאכילת עראי דפת:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:10:1.english: "Two (or) three" - Rashi explained: Two or three times he puts into his mouth — morcel [morsel] in Old French. And there are books in which it is written, "Two [or] three egg[-bulks]," and it is all one [and the same], as is proven below regarding [the question], "Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Yosef and Abaye?" — for the measure of the gullet [a swallow] is an egg[-bulk]. And at the end, [the Gemara] concludes: "Like that which a young scholar tastes and goes to the lecture," which is a mouthful, that is, an egg[-bulk]. And this measure applies specifically to bread; for fruit does not require a sukka, as [the Gemara] concludes in the final chapter of Yoma (79b and there), that an established meal of them is like casual eating of bread.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:12:1.hebrew: אבל שינת קבע לא - והא דאמרי' פרק במה טומנין (שבת דף מט. ושם): "תפילין צריכין גוף נקי כאלישע בעל כנפים", ואמר אביי: "שלא יפיח בהן", ורבא אמר: "שלא ישן בהן" — לאו דשרי אביי לישן, דהא אסר אביי גופיה הכא! אלא קסבר: אע"פ שאינו זהיר בשינה כאלישע — מניחן, כיון דזהיר שלא יפיח; דשינה גופה אינה אלא גזרה שמא יפיח:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:12:1.english: "But substantial sleep is not permitted" - And that which we say in the chapter entitled Bameh Tomnin (Shabbat 49a and there): "Phylacteries require a clean body like Elisha, the man of wings," and Abaye said: "That one not pass gas in them," and Rava said: "That one not sleep in them" — this is not that Abaye permits sleeping, for Abaye himself prohibited it here! Rather, he maintains: Even though one is not cautious regarding sleep like Elisha, one may don them, since one is cautious not to pass gas; for sleep itself is only a decree lest one pass gas.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:15:1.hebrew: הישן בתפילין - מתוך הלשון משמע דרבי יעקב שרי אפי' שינת קבע, דאי לאו הכי, במאי פליגי? וי"ל, דכולהו מודו בשינת קבע דאסיר, ופליגי במילתיה דרבי נתן דבסמוך — דשרי לישן בתפילין ביום, שאין דרכו לישן שינת קבע, ובלילה חולץ אפילו לשינת עראי, דלמא ממליך וישן שינת קבע; ור' יעקב לא חייש דלמא ממליך:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:15:1.english: One who sleeps with phylacteries - From the wording, it is implied that Rabbi Ya’akov permits even substantial sleep, for if not so, in what do they disagree? And one can say that all agree that substantial sleep is forbidden, and they disagree regarding the statement of Rabbi Natan [cited] nearby, who permits sleeping with phylacteries during the day, when it is not one’s habit to sleep a substantial sleep, whereas at night he removes [them] even for a brief nap, lest he reconsider and sleep a substantial sleep; and Rabbi Ya’akov is not concerned lest he reconsider.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:1:1.hebrew: חתן פטור מקריאת שמע - דטריד, ושאר בני חופה חייבין — לית להו להני תנאי "העוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה", כדפירש בקונט'. וקשיא: דאי לית להו, א"כ יתחייב חתן בסוכה! ומשמע דבחתן פוטר יותר מת"ק. לכך נראה, דקסבר: חתן אין יכול לכוין דעתו כלל, אפי' בפסוק ראשון; אבל שאר בני חופה יכולין לכוין. ואקריאת שמע לחודיה קאי, ובכולהו אחריני מודי לת"ק:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:1:1.english: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema - Because he is preoccupied; and the other members of the wedding party are obligated [because] these Tannaim do not hold [the principle that] one who is engaged in a mitzvah is exempt from [another] mitzvah, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres. And this is difficult: For if they do not hold [it], if so, let the groom be obligated in [the mitzvah of] sukkah! And [furthermore], it implies that regarding the groom he exempts [him] even more than the first Tanna. Therefore, it appears that he holds: A groom cannot concentrate his mind at all, even for the first verse; but the other members of the wedding party are able to concentrate. And [Rabbi Sheila's statement] applies only to the recitation of Shema, whereas in all other [matters] he agrees with the first Tanna.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:2:1.hebrew: ומכל מצות האמורות בתורה - מאי דאיצטריך למיחשב הני — אגב דחשבינהו בברייתא קמייתא:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:2:1.english: "And from all mitzvot that are mentioned in the Torah" - [The reason] that it was necessary to enumerate these — [it is] because it enumerated them in the earlier baraita.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:3:1.hebrew: הולכי דרכים ביום - כל זה נפקא מ"תשבו כעין תדורו", שכשם שאדם בביתו אינו נמנע מלצאת לדרך. וכן מצטער דפטרו לעיל מן הסוכה — היינו מ"תשבו כעין תדורו", דאין אדם דר במקום שמצטער:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:3:1.english: Travelers during the day: All this is derived from "You shall dwell as you reside" — for just as a person in his home does not refrain from setting out on a journey, [so too during the Festival]. And likewise, [regarding] one who is in distress, whom they exempted earlier from the sukka, that is [also derived] from "You shall dwell as you reside," as a person does not reside in a place where he is in distress.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:3:2.english: "And are obligated at night" - [This applies] when a person lodges at night in a settlement.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:6:1.hebrew: פרצה קוראה לגנב - לאו משום דלית ליה לרבא דרשה ד"תשבו כעין תדורו", דברייתא היא לקמן בפירקין (סוכה דף כח:):
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:6:1.english: A breach summons the thief - [This is] not because Rava does not accept the exposition of "reside as you dwell," for it is a baraita later in our chapter (Sukkah 28b).

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:7:1.hebrew: ואפילו חש בעיניו - אע"פ שאין בו סכנת עין; דסכנת אבר כסכנת נפשות, אפילו לחלל עליו את השבת, כדמוכח פרק אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כח.) גבי עין שמרדה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:7:1.english: "And even [one who] feels pain in his eyes" - [This means] even though there is no danger to the eye; for danger to a limb is like danger to life, [permitting one] even to desecrate Shabbat for it, as is proved in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 28b) regarding an eye that rebelled.

Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:8:1.hebrew: משום בקי - ואע"פ שבפ"ק (דף יא.) דרש רבה בר רב הונא: "מותר לישן בכילת חתנים, אע"פ שיש לה גג, ואע"פ שגבוהה עשרה" — אין הלכה (כרבה), כדפירשתי שם:
Tosafot on Sukkah 26a:8:1.english: Due to gnats - And even though in the first chapter (11a) Rabba bar Rav Huna expounded: "It is permitted to sleep in a bridal canopy even though it has a roof and even though it is ten [handbreadths] high," the halakha is not in accordance with Rabba, as I explained there.
